papers.title: Gravitational-Wave Echoes and Greybody Cutoff from Logarithmic Throats at a Marginal-Trapping Threshold
papers.summary: When a static, spherically symmetric configuration is brought close to a marginal-trapping threshold, it develops a long throat. As the nondegenerate minimum of $F=1-2m/r$ approaches zero, $F\simeqΔ+β(r-R_M)^2$, the proper length across the throat grows as $-\lnΔ/\sqrtβ$, even though the local curvature stays finite. We study how axial gravitational waves propagate in an effective model of this throat, in which the lapse is parametrized as $N\propto F^{s/2}$. For $s>0$ the throat acts as a cavity behind the angular-momentum barrier, and waves come back out as echoes spaced by $T_{\rm echo}\simeq2Λ+δ\proptoΔ^{-s/2}$, where $Λ$ is the optical length of the throat and $δ$ does not depend on $Δ$. We study four-dimensional, matter-supported quasi-black holes in which a regular centre caps the near-AdS$_2$ throat. These configurations provide a simplified model for investigating capped throats in horizonless microstate geometries. The echo delay in this model is controlled by the inverse redshift near the bottom of the throat, as in capped microstate geometries. This differs from thin-shell gravastars and wormholes, where the delay grows only logarithmically with the distance to the would-be horizon. Time-domain evolutions confirm the $Δ^{-s/2}$ scaling over three decades in $Δ$; for $s=0$ the throat becomes part of the barrier and no distinct echo appears. The barrier also imposes a greybody cutoff on the reflected spectrum, $1-Γ\simeq e^{-(ω-f)/T}$, where $T$ is fixed by the curvature of the barrier and does not depend on the surface gravity of any horizon behind it. In this model, the prompt signal is the same whether the interior contains a horizon or a reflecting throat. In the horizonless case, however, the transmitted wave returns as echoes, restoring the high-frequency part of the full reflected spectrum.

papers.title: The Conditional CMB Visibility of High-Redshift X-Ray Cavities in Galaxy clusters
papers.summary: At high redshift, the cosmic microwave background (CMB) both cools relativistic leptons and provides seed photons for inverse-Compton (IC) X-ray emission. These two effects link the particle content of a bubble directly to the soft X-ray depression used to identify a cavity. We derive a physical criterion connecting lepton cooling, bubble volume, enthalpy evolution, and 0.5--2 keV X-ray visibility, while separating intrinsic filling of the X-ray depression from detector-dependent cavity recovery. For uncooled electron populations described by a power law with spectral index $s=2.5$, minimum Lorentz factor $100\leqγ_{\min}\leq1000$, and maximum Lorentz factor $γ_{\max}=10^5$, the measured atmosphere of the testbed high-redshift cluster SPT-CL J2215$-$3537 requires 0.6--1.2\% of the pressure in radiating leptons to fill the soft-band deficit. Across the full tested ranges of $s$, $γ_{\min}$, and atmospheric properties, the required fraction is 0.2--3.7\%. Complete loss of this component reduces the enthalpy by less than 3\% relative to an otherwise identical adiabatic bubble at the same pressure. A low-cutoff control with $γ_{\min}=10$ and $s=3$ instead requires 18.9\%, identifying the poorly constrained low-energy spectrum as the main physical uncertainty. For a fixed atmosphere and spectrum, the required fraction scales as $(1+z)^{-4}$. The declining-pressure tracks show that the X-ray deficit can cross the adopted detection threshold while the enthalpy deficit remains below 0.4\%; the time of this transition depends on the assumed pressure history. Thus, high-redshift cavity visibility depends on both the surrounding atmosphere and the pressure-carrying particle spectrum. This criterion provides the physical basis for an instrument-specific recovery analysis.

papers.title: The unresolved high-mass frontier of the black hole Fundamental Plane
papers.summary: Accreting black holes follow a Fundamental Plane (FP) linking radio and X-ray luminosities to black hole mass, but whether this relation changes in the ultramassive regime, above $\sim10^{10}\,\Msun$, remains unresolved. Brightest cluster galaxies (BCGs) provide the most direct access to this regime, although earlier claims of enhanced radio emission relied largely on heterogeneous nuclear measurements and black hole masses inferred from host-galaxy proxies. We recalibrate the forward FP using galaxies with direct dynamical mass measurements and reassess the evidence for a high-mass radio excess using the available BCG data. We find that the archival proxy-mass sample cannot uniquely establish such an excess because the inferred signal remains sensitive to the mass calibration and radio-selection properties of the sample. Using mock observing programs, we further show that the predictive width measured from existing observations makes a high-mass transition difficult to both detect and localize with present samples. The existing data therefore provide no compelling evidence for a distinct high-mass branch of the FP. Resolving this question will require a substantially larger, uniformly selected sample of galaxies with direct black hole masses and matched, preferably quasi-simultaneous, nuclear radio and X-ray measurements. A focused pilot survey of several dozen direct-mass systems would provide a practical first step toward establishing whether the required precision is achievable.
papers.comment: 17 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for Publications in PASP

papers.title: Influence of $Δ$ resonances in hyperonic neutron stars on gravitational-wave inspiral signatures
papers.summary: The composition of dense matter in neutron star interiors remains uncertain, with the possible appearance of the non-strange $Δ$ resonances providing an important source of theoretical uncertainty. In this work, we investigate the gravitational wave signatures of hyperonic neutron stars containing $Δ$ baryons within a density-dependent relativistic mean-field framework based on the DDME2 parametrization. Within this framework, the baryons interact among themselves via mesons. For $Δ$ baryons, the interaction is uncertain to date. We investigate how variations of the scalar and vector $Δ-$meson couplings, subject to \(x_{σΔ}-x_{ωΔ}=0.2\), modify the tidal properties and inspiral gravitational-wave signals. We find that the allowed variation in the $Δ-σ$ coupling leads to substantial changes in the tidal properties of the neutron stars, which in turn leave distinct imprints on the gravitational-wave waveforms, particularly in their frequency evolution, accumulated phase, and strain amplitude. These waveform differences arise through changes in tidal deformability and are not unique signatures of $Δ$ resonances. Future gravitational-wave observations may therefore constrain the $Δ-$meson couplings within the adopted dense-matter framework, subject to degeneracies with alternative EOS models.
papers.comment: 16 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for publication in Phys. Rev. D

papers.title: Polarization and Burst Properties of the Repeating FRB~20240209A in a Quiescent Elliptical Host
papers.summary: We report polarimetric observations of the repeating fast radio burst (FRB) source FRB 20240209A with the Green Bank Telescope at L band and 800 MHz. This source has previously been associated with a quiescent elliptical galaxy with a mass-weighted stellar age of approximately 11 Gyr. We detected three bursts, and the brightest burst resolves into eight components that drift toward lower frequencies. The bursts have mutually consistent rotation measures (RMs), and the small extragalactic RM agrees with the low RM predicted from the small host-galaxy dispersion measure ($\mathrm{DM}_\mathrm{host}$). The linear polarization fraction decreases toward lower frequencies within the brightest burst, consistent with depolarization by an RM scatter of $σ_\mathrm{RM}\simeq3.5$ rad m$^{-2}$. This RM scatter is comparable to those of several repeaters in star-forming galaxies. Therefore, FRBs in both star-forming and old, quiescent hosts can reside in relatively complex magneto-ionic environments, which suggests that FRB sources may form through multiple channels.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 7 figures, 1 table. Accepted for publication in ApJ

papers.title: posterior-landscape: morphological feature finding in two-dimensional probability densities
papers.summary: We present posterior-landscape, a Python framework to identify and characterize morphological features in two-dimensional probability densities. The framework combines concepts from topological data analysis, statistical density-ridge estimation, and scale-space image analysis. It extracts localized concentrations, valleys, ridges, and changes of slope; for Bayesian reconstructions, it propagates uncertainty in feature recovery, geometry, and correspondence across posteriors. The framework also connects two-dimensional structures to features in one-dimensional marginals, and quantifies their correlation with other inferred parameters. We validate the method on controlled densities, and demonstrate its use on gravitational-wave population reconstructions, where it provides a systematic way to identify and interpret population features and assess which ones carry information relevant for cosmology. The resulting catalogues also offer a common morphological representation for future comparisons between predictions and population reconstructions.

papers.title: A Candidate Binary Microlensing Event in the 2018 Gamma-Ray Flare of 3C 279
papers.summary: The April 2018 gamma-ray flare of the flat-spectrum radio quasar 3C~279 exhibited sharp peaks within a broader outburst. Its rapid substructure was previously attributed to magnetic reconnection. Motivated by its distinctive temporal profile within our comparison sample of bright blazar flares and its resemblance to caustic-crossing features in optical microlensing events, we investigate a finite-source binary-microlensing interpretation. A jointly fitted model of binary-lens magnification, a smooth intrinsic flare, and Gaussian-process variability reproduces the principal double-peaked structure of the GeV light curve. The adopted local solution has a binary mass ratio of $q\simeq0.098$ and an Einstein timescale of $t_{\rm E}\simeq0.327$~d. The absolute lens mass and projected source radius depend on the lens distance and relative proper motion. The fitted geometry can correspond to a Galactic planetary-mass binary or an intervening stellar or substellar system, with different physical source sizes in each case. We present binary microlensing as a testable interpretation of this event, with the finite-source structure offering a potential probe of the compact GeV-emitting region.
papers.comment: 12 pages, 7 figures

papers.title: From photons to neutrinos : Advancing multi-messenger modeling with Gammapy
papers.summary: In recent years, several astrophysical objects have been identified as potential multi-messenger photon-neutrino emitters. New instruments dedicated to the study of these two messengers have been and are still being built, achieving unprecedented sensitivity. This observational improvement increases the need for more sophisticated and precise analysis tools. Multi-wavelength and multi-messenger data fitting is crucial to constrain astrophysical models of particle acceleration and radiation mechanisms at work in these extreme environments. In this contribution, we present a novel framework dedicated to multi-wavelength and multi-messenger modeling, built within the open-source software Gammapy. The framework enables data analysis from optical up to very-high-energy gamma rays, and fitting physical models directly to instrumental counts in these wavebands, without the need of computing flux points. Focusing on blazars as a first example of a multi-messenger candidate, we showcase the performance of this tool in constraining multi-wavelength emission models, and how it reduces fitting biases. We show the results of a leptonic model that can be fitted on the fly, due to the short computing time needed. For more computing-intensive emission codes, we explore a grid-fitting approach. We evaluate the performance of the new fitting tool and present its first application to leptonic modeling of blazars. By fitting directly on photon and neutrino events, this novel approach will enable, for the first time, statistically sound constraints on the physics of multi-messenger sources.
papers.comment: 5 pages, 5 figures, conference proceedings of Gamma 2026

papers.title: What kinds of strong star--black-hole encounters in AGN disks occur, and how often?
papers.summary: Disks surrounding active galactic nuclei contain many stars and black holes, which will inevitably encounter one another. The outcome of these encounters depends on how closely and how rapidly the bodies meet. Extending previous studies, we account for initial relative velocities seeded by stochastic effects in the disk; incorporate a strong-encounter cross-section accounting for single- and binary-mediated interactions computed via direct two-body (Hill) or three-body (isolated) interactions; and present a repeated-encounter model accounting both for energy loss due to stellar encounters as well as the SMBH tidal field. We convolve our encounter model with a parametric family of natal stellar and binary populations, focused on varying binary fraction and period distribution. In our fiducial disk model, even though single-single interactions supply most encounters, binary-mediated interactions supply 68% of collisions; most encounters are well-approximated as parabolic; and stochastically-driven relative velocities are comparatively substantial and driven by gravitational perturbations from disk fluctuations and neighboring bodies. Our tools are ready to use in downstream applications, including several easily-expressed semianalytic approximations to key interaction phenomena.
papers.comment: 34 pages, plus 9-page supplemental material

papers.title: Evolutionary tracks and isochrones of the inverse Hall cascade
papers.summary: Decaying MHD turbulence can exhibit an inverse cascade, which means that the height of the spectrum of magnetic energy in the subinertial range increases with time. However, there is evidence for a resistive dependence of the inverse transfer speed. It is unclear whether this is caused by reconnection, which is known to depend on resistivity. Here, we show that in the Hall cascade, where no momentum equation is solved, and the induction term is replaced by what corresponds to the negative Lorentz force in MHD, there is still a resistive dependence of the inverse transfer speed, but no such dependence is found for an analogous numerical reconnection experiment. This suggests that the resistive dependence of the inverse transfer speed is not necessarily related to reconnection.
papers.comment: 16 pages, 9 figures, 3 tables, submitted to J. Plasma Phys

papers.title: KM3-230213A: The Highest-Energy Cosmic Neutrino
papers.summary: High-energy neutrinos provide a unique probe of the most extreme non-thermal processes in the Universe. The detection of the ultra-high-energy neutrino event KM3-230213A by the KM3NeT neutrino telescope, with an inferred parent-neutrino energy of O(10^17 eV), represents a major step forward in neutrino astronomy. In this review, we summarize the main properties of the event and discuss its interpretation within different astrophysical and cosmological scenarios, including active galactic nuclei, transient sources, and cosmogenic neutrinos, highlighting the role of multi-messenger constraints. Despite extensive follow-up observations, no unambiguous electromagnetic counterpart has been identified, and the event remains in tension with the absence of comparable detections in other experiments. This situation leaves open the possibility of more complex source scenarios or contributions from physics beyond the Standard Model. We also discuss the implications for the ultra-high-energy neutrino landscape and the prospects for future observations with next-generation detectors. KM3-230213A provides a unique opportunity to probe particle acceleration and neutrino production at energies far beyond the reach of terrestrial experiments.
papers.comment: 24 pages, 13 figures, 1 table. Published in Physics and the Cosmos (2026)

papers.title: Inverse Gertsenshteǐn-Zel'dovich Effect in Time-Independent Electromagnetic Field
papers.summary: The inverse Gertsenshteǐn-Zel'dovich effect describes the conversion of gravitational waves into electromagnetic waves in the presence of a background electromagnetic field. This effect has primarily been studied for constant background electromagnetic fields. In this work, we develop a general formalism for calculating the components of the electric and magnetic fields induced by the passage of a gravitational wave through a spatially varying, time-independent background electromagnetic field. The formalism accommodates all six possible polarization modes of gravitational waves. We illustrate its applicability through several examples, including gravitational waves propagating through constant and spatially varying electromagnetic fields. We further investigate the electromagnetic signals generated by the passage of gravitational waves through astrophysical magnetic fields, particularly those associated with neutron stars and magnetars. By connecting gravitational waves and electromagnetic waves--two essential messengers of multi-messenger astronomy--the inverse Gertsenshteǐn-Zel'dovich effect offers a promising framework for both gravitational-wave detection and astrophysical observations. The formalism developed here may therefore find applications in the design of high-frequency gravitational-wave detectors and in the investigation of high-energy astrophysical electromagnetic signals.
papers.comment: 17 pages, 3 figures

papers.title: VERITAS Limits on Dark Matter Annihilation in the Galactic Center Halo
papers.summary: Well-motivated models of particle dark matter predict its self-annihilation into Standard Model end states, which may be detected by particle detectors or telescopes. We conduct an indirect dark matter search using gamma rays detected by the VERITAS telescope from within $2^\circ$ of the Galactic Center. A template-based approach is used for background estimation, increasing our sensitivity to sources of gamma-ray emission with spatial extents comparable to the $3.5^\circ$ VERITAS field of view. The analysis benefits from data taken exclusively at large zenith angles, which results in an increased effective area at energies above ~1 TeV, compared to small zenith angle observations. No significant gamma-ray signal is observed in the search region, resulting in upper limits on the end-state-dependent dark matter annihilation cross sections. Cross sections as low as $\langle σ_\text{ann} v\rangle = 1.77\times 10^{-25} \text{ cm}^3 \text{ s}^{-1}$ are excluded at 95% confidence assuming complete annihilation into $τ^+ τ^-$, an Einasto profile, and a dark matter mass of 1 TeV.
papers.journal_ref: Archer et al. 2026, Phys. Rev. D 114, 083044

papers.title: Tidal disruption or plunge: the role of neutron star internal structure in black hole-neutron star mergers
papers.summary: The outcome of black hole--neutron star (BHNS) mergers is studied using a general-relativistic mass-shedding condition in the Kerr spacetime, which determines the tidal-disruption radius from the mass ratio, the black hole (BH) spin, the neutron star (NS) compactness, and the ratio of central to average density, $η=\frac{ρ_{c}}{\barρ}$. Comparing this radius with the innermost stable circular orbit, we map the boundary between tidal disruption and plunge for two relativistic mean-field equations of state (EOSs) and for an ensemble of about $10^4$ agnostic EOSs spanning the current uncertainty in the NS radius. We find that the disruption threshold is set mainly by the compactness, but NSs with the same compactness and different $η$ can have different outcomes. Using the tidal disruption radius, we construct a remnant-mass model calibrated against 70 numerical-relativity simulations, which reproduces the remnant mass with an accuracy comparable to existing fits. Applying the disruption criterion and the remnant model to GW200105, GW200115, and the candidate BHNS event GW230529, we find that GW200105 and GW200115 are consistent with a direct plunge. GW230529 lies close to the disruption threshold and may have undergone marginal disruption, leaving only a low-mass remnant.
papers.comment: 15 pages, 6 figures

papers.title: The first mass peak of merging black holes from core binding energies and jet-driven explosions
papers.summary: We show that the jittering-jets explosion mechanism (JJEM) can qualitatively reproduce the shape of the black hole (BH) mass distribution observed by LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA and quantitatively reproduce the peak around $M_{p1} \simeq 10 M_\odot$. To show this, we construct a toy model that captures the JJEM physics that explodes all massive stars, even when BHs form. According to the JJEM, BHs form when the star's binding energy is large, implying a massive progenitor with initial mass $M_i \gtrsim 25 M_\odot$, and when jets are launched along a fixed axis, implying a rapidly rotating pre-collapse stellar core. In this case, the jets are launched along the core's angular momentum and are inefficient at removing mass near the equatorial plane; when the stellar binding energy is large, a large fraction of the equatorial mass is accreted to form the BH. The toy model includes two parameters: the threshold binding energy in the core for BH formation and the jet opening angle along the poles. Although our finding is encouraging for the JJEM, future hydrodynamical simulations must determine the exact condition for BH formation in the JJEM and the BH mass.
papers.comment: Will submit to PASP in two days to allow for comments; 11 pages, 5 figures

papers.title: RAKI: High-Order Alternative Finite Differences for General Relativistic Magnetohydrodynamics
papers.summary: Binary neutron star (BNS) and black hole--neutron star mergers are among the most important multimessenger sources. Observations of these events could provide valuable insights into several unresolved phenomena, ranging from the efficiency of magnetic field amplification during and after mergers to the formation of magnetars and jets. Understanding these phenomena requires accurate modelling of magnetic field evolution, which remains a challenge for state-of-the-art general relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (GRMHD) simulations. In this work, we present \texttt{RAKI} (Relativistic Astrophysics Code Implementation of the Alternative Finite Difference Approach for GRMHD), the first GRMHD code to simulate BNS mergers using high-order alternative finite-difference methods with adaptive-order WENO (AFD-WENO-AO) reconstruction and a fully non-staggered, node-centred vector-potential formulation. The code achieves up to ninth-order convergence in smooth test problems while accurately capturing discontinuities. In magnetised Tolman--Oppenheimer--Volkoff (TOV) star tests, \texttt{RAKI} retains $99.2$ per cent of the initial maximum magnetic field strength over ${\sim}2$ ms, exhibiting an order of magnitude less magnetic field loss than a reference GRMHD code at the same resolution. In BNS merger simulations, fifth-order AFD-WENO-AO reconstruction yields approximately third-order convergence of the gravitational-wave phase in both magnetised and unmagnetised models. The discrete no-monopole constraint is preserved to machine precision without staggered grids, even during BNS mergers with moving refinement regions. These results establish \texttt{RAKI} as a high-order, non-staggered GRMHD framework for accurate modelling of magnetic field evolution in neutron star mergers and its implications for multimessenger astrophysics.
papers.comment: 21 pages, 12 figures, 1 table

papers.title: Search for Cosmic Rays in GRANDProto300
papers.summary: GRANDProto300 is a prototype array of the GRAND experiment, designed to validate the technique of autonomous radio-detection of astroparticles by detecting cosmic rays with energies between 10$^{17} - 10^{18.5}$ eV. This observation will further enable the study of the Galactic-to-extragalactic source transition region. Between November 2024 and June 2025, 46 antennas were operational, and since July 2025, 63 antennas have been collecting data stably. We present here our cosmic-ray search pipeline, that involves several filtering steps: (1) exclusion of clustered (in time and space) noise events, (2) polarization cut, (3) zenith arrival cut, and (4) delay in expected trigger cut. The efficiency is evaluated on the latest batch of data from July 2025 to October 2025. Additionally, we present an identification layer that is being developed: a CNN-based algorithm to discriminate between noise and cosmic-ray signals, using signal traces. We present the accuracy of our model, trained both on simulations and on real cosmic-ray signal datasets.
papers.comment: Presented at the 60th Rencontres de Moriond on Very High Energy Phenomena in the Universe (Moriond VHEPU 2026). 4 pages, 1 figure

papers.title: Feeding or Fleeing: The Impact of Enhanced Early Black Hole Growth on Circumgalactic Clumps at $z > 6$
papers.summary: The circumgalactic medium (CGM) of massive high-redshift galaxies contains inflowing filamentary gas, recycled material, and feedback-driven outflows. We investigate the formation and evolution of dense CGM clumps in two cosmological zoom-in simulations of the same massive halo at $z > 6$: the fiducial Fable model and the modified Fable-SE model, which includes enhanced early black hole growth through mild super-Eddington accretion. We identify dense gas clumps in the CGM and follow their gas properties, stellar content, and radial evolution across cosmic time. At the resolution probed here, the two simulations show broadly similar distributions of clump gas mass, gas size and associated stellar mass. Instead, the clump populations differ mainly in their abundance, metallicity, and radial evolution. Fable-SE produces substantially more metal-enriched clumps, including an outward-moving population during the strong AGN-driven blow-out phase at $z \lesssim 7$. These systems are associated with disturbed HI-rich gas and relatively high gas densities, linking the increased prevalence of dense, metal-enriched CGM structures in Fable-SE to its stronger AGN-driven blow-out phase. Although inward migration dominates overall, Fable-SE also contains an outward-moving clump population during the blow-out phase, with some clumps moving beyond the virial radius. Our results therefore indicate that the distribution of dense CGM clumps around massive high-redshift galaxies reflects both filamentary accretion and feedback-driven CGM evolution, with strong early AGN activity associated with the outward migration of dense, metal-enriched gas structures containing relatively cool gas.
papers.comment: Comments and suggestions welcome prior to submission to MNRAS

papers.title: The Pointing Error Due To Laser Propagation in Space Plasma for TianQin Gravitational Wave Detection
papers.summary: TianQin, a space-borne gravitational wave observatory, is designed to detect gravitational-wave signals via laser interferometry. As the inhomogeneous space plasma surrounds the inter-satellite laser links, the propagation of the laser in space plasma can introduce pointing error noise. In this work, we quantitatively assess the effect of plasma on the pointing accuracy of TQ's inter-satellite laser links. We employ a magnetohydrodynamic model to simulate the plasma distribution around the TQ orbit for different orbital orientations. Using the fourth-order Runge-Kutta method to conduct the ray-tracing calculations over a TQ orbital cycle under a solar wind dynamic pressure close to the 23-year average, we find that the plasma-induced laser deflection angle and pointing eccentricity are on the order of $10^{-20} \ \mathrm{rad}$ and picometers, respectively. These values are significantly lower than TQ's requirements. Our results demonstrate that the impact of space plasma on TQ's pointing error is negligible in moderate space weather conditions, indicating a positive outlook for the TQ mission.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 7 figures Published in Space Weather

papers.title: The Disk Awakens: IXPE's Sequel Observation of GS 1354-64 Suggests Changing-Look Behavior in the Steep-Power-Law State
papers.summary: After decades of only failed transitions, the black hole X-ray binary GS 1354-64 has undergone a complete outburst again. We present its first X-ray polarimetric investigation in the fading steep-power-law (SPL) state, following an earlier intermediate-state IXPE campaign during the same outburst. The 2-8 keV emission has a polarization degree (PD) of 2.3 +/- 0.2% and polarization angle (PA) of 5 +/- 3 degrees. Compared with the intermediate state, where PD=3.9 +0.3/-0.2% and PA=-2 +/-2 degrees, the broadband PD is lower while the PA remains consistent. The intermediate-state type-C quasi-periodic oscillation state has also disappeared, marking a major reconfiguration of the accretion flow. Assuming a distance of 7 kpc, the observed the intensity drop from 2.5% to 1.6% of the Eddington luminosity over 10.2 days is punctuated by several broad hour-to-day-scale troughs, tracing two distinct tracks in hardness-intensity space. Simultaneous spectroscopy shows the troughs' spectra contains a cooler disk with smaller apparent normalization, while no change in the Compton component's photon index or normalization is required between tracks. The model-independent analysis identifies a steeper increase in PD with energy outside the troughs, yielding G_E=1.5 +/- 0.2%/keV, compared with G_E=0.7 +0.3/-0.5%/keV during the troughs. Their duration and spectropolarimetric morphology distinguish the troughs from traditional short absorption dips seen in X-ray binaries, providing a possible stellar-mass analog of the recurrent accretion changes that drive "changing-look" behavior in supermassive black hole systems.
papers.comment: 23 pages, 10 figures, Submitted to ApJ

papers.title: A universal relation predicts the observed reversal of a supernova chirp
papers.summary: Superluminous supernovae, among the brightest stellar explosions, are thought to be powered by newborn magnetars. One such event, SN 2024afav, ``chirped'', displaying sinusoidal, increasing-frequency ($P(99\textrm{ d})\sim39\pm8$ d to $P(166\textrm{ d})\sim17\pm5$ d) light-curve modulations. The model explaining this chirp, a precessing disk falling onto the dimming magnetar, generalizes to a normalization-independent universal relation between the period derivative and the dimming rate of the light curve. Applied to the published chirp alone, with the spin-down time measured from the unmodulated light curve, the relation predicts that the chirp must halt near $t \approx 150$ d and reverse. With continued follow-up of SN 2024afav, we report the discovery of five new modulations in which the chirp reverses ($P(177\textrm{ d})\sim24\pm4$ d to $P(208\textrm{ d})\sim38\pm2$ d) at $t=147\pm3$ d, as predicted. Applied to chirping events from upcoming surveys, the relation could identify the precession mechanism and disk physics of each engine.
papers.comment: 17 pages, 8 figures

papers.title: XRISM/Resolve Study of Large Scale Properties in Tycho's Supernova Remnant
papers.summary: Resolve, the microcalorimeter array aboard the X-Ray Imaging and Spectroscopy Mission (XRISM), provides an unprecedented spectral view of Tycho's Supernova Remnant (SNR). We fit the X-ray spectra of the five public archival XRISM observations of the SNR with a multi-component non-equilibrium ionization plasma model assuming spherical expansion and a uniform abundance pattern. For pointings away from the center of the object, we divide each into three spectra based on angular distance from the remnant's geometric center and fit all three simultaneously with the center-pointing observation. We tie elemental abundances together across all model components. We find that pseudo-spherical expansion fits well the Tycho SNR in the regions where Resolve has observed, although iron appears slower on the approaching side than the receding side. We also find that a close-to-uniform abundance pattern across the SNR is consistent with these data.
papers.comment: 14 pages, 5 figures, 6 tables, submitted to ApJ

papers.title: Gravitational lensing of gravitational waves by a Kerr black hole
papers.summary: We simulate the gravitational lensing of gravitational waves (GWs) by a Kerr black hole using a $(1+1)$-dimensional time-domain mode-sum approach. To enable efficient explicit time evolution, we implement a localized hyperboloidal foliation combined with a static field redefinition, ensuring bounded characteristic speeds across an extended, uniform tortoise-coordinate grid. Incident GW initial data are constructed by projecting a plane-wave Weyl tensor onto the Kinnersley tetrad. Through local spin-dyad rotations and Wigner $D$-matrix transformations, our framework accommodates both idealized wave packets and realistic binary coalescence signals at arbitrary incidence and polarization angles. To accurately resolve the lensed waveforms, we evolve over $68,000$ coupled $(j,m)$ modes. Our results reveal that a Kerr black hole acts as a diffraction-limited thick lens, focusing GWs into a forward beam. For idealized wave packets, the primary prompt pulse exhibits a spin-independent transverse Gaussian profile, whereas the subsequent lensing coda is sensitive to the black hole's spin. For binary coalescence signals, strong-field lensing substantially modifies the post-merger ringdown. However, the lensed inspiral and merger phases in Kerr and Schwarzschild backgrounds are virtually identical, yielding waveform mismatches below $2.2\times10^{-5}$ across various inclinations and polarizations. These findings demonstrate that non-spinning Schwarzschild models provide an accurate and computationally economical surrogate to search for strong-field lensing signatures with current ground-based detectors.
papers.comment: 26 pages, 5 figures

papers.title: Harmonic brightness oscillations point to magnetar giant flares in rare short gamma-ray bursts
papers.summary: Kilohertz quasi-periodic oscillations (QPOs) have been observed in a few rare gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), but their physical origin remains uncertain. We reanalyze the two short GRBs with reported kilohertz QPOs, GRB 910711 and GRB 200415A, and find evidence for possible harmonic-like organization around a characteristic frequency scale near 360 hertz. The similar harmonic-like pattern in GRB 910711 and in the confirmed magnetar giant flare (MGF) event GRB 200415A, including features extending above 4 kilohertz, points to timing phenomenology on frequency scales relevant to magnetar oscillation modes. The temporal and spectral similarities between the two events and the difficulty of explaining these features in merger-driven scenarios favor an MGF-like interpretation of GRB 910711. This timing phenomenology may therefore provide an additional observational handle, complementary to spectral, temporal, and localization information, for distinguishing rare MGF-like transients from merger-driven GRBs.
papers.comment: 57 pages, 9 figures; Authors' version of the article published in Science Advances, available at https://www.science.org/doi/abs/10.1126/sciadv.aee6388

papers.title: Simultaneous Real-Color Time-Domain Survey of the Coma Field with the Multi-channel Photometric Survey Telescope (Mephisto)
papers.summary: We present the results from a high-cadence, multi-channel time-domain survey targeting the Coma galaxy cluster, utilizing the newly commissioned 1.6-m Multi-channel Photometric Survey Telescope (Mephisto). Mephisto's pioneering mosaic focal-plane design enables strictly simultaneous imaging in three distinct optical bands ($u/v, g/r, i/z$). This unique capability allows for the extraction of true, instantaneous spectral energy distributions (SEDs) of fast-evolving transients. Our survey continuously monitors a 20-square-degree footprint centered on the Coma cluster. By strategically targeting this massive local structure, we exploit cosmic anisotropy to significantly amplify the volumetric discovery rate of stellar explosions. During the initial six-month pilot operation, we successfully detected and tracked nine new supernovae (SNe). Remarkably, our high-cadence, multi-band strategy allowed us to capture ultra-early rising light curves and pre-discovery signals (e.g., SN 2026dyr) hours to days prior to formal discovery alerts. These instantaneous early-phase colors allow us to reconstruct intrinsic SEDs without temporal interpolation, providing reliable constraints on the physical parameters of early supernova (SN) evolution. Furthermore, our observed supernova yield shows good agreement with theoretical forecasts based on local stellar mass and star-formation rate overdensities. These pilot results validate the efficiency of the Mephisto Coma survey, demonstrating its objective capability to systematically explore the local transient population and provide rapid optical localizations for future multi-messenger events.
